1: # Antigravity Plugin Architecture Guide
2: 
3: > Lessons learned from building and deploying the `bug-fixer-loop` plugin.  
4: > This document captures the practical architecture of Antigravity plugins — what works, what breaks, and why.
5: 
6: ---
7: 
8: ## Table of Contents
9: 
10: - [Core Concepts](#core-concepts)
11: - [Directory Layout](#directory-layout)
12: - [Discovery & Loading](#discovery--loading)
13: - [The Immutable Plugin Root Principle](#the-immutable-plugin-root-principle)
14: - [Configuration Management](#configuration-management)
15: - [Hooks](#hooks)
16: - [Rules](#rules)
17: - [Skills](#skills)
18: - [Sidecars & Dispatchers](#sidecars--dispatchers)
19:   - [How Antigravity Discovers Sidecars](#how-antigravity-discovers-sidecars)
20:   - [Sidecar Manifest](#sidecar-manifest-sidecarjson)
21:   - [Sidecar Execution Model](#sidecar-execution-model)
22:   - [The `env` Block is Critical](#the-env-block-is-critical)
23:   - [Sidecar Templates vs Installed Sidecars](#sidecar-templates-vs-installed-sidecars)
24:   - [Sidecar Lifecycle & Failure Modes](#sidecar-lifecycle--failure-modes)
25:   - [Dispatcher Architecture](#dispatcher-architecture-the-non-llm-control-plane)
26: - [Circuit Breakers](#circuit-breakers)
27: - [Installation Architecture](#installation-architecture)
28: - [Anti-Patterns](#anti-patterns-learned-the-hard-way)
29: - [Multi-Project Support](#multi-project-support)
30: - [Checklist: Shipping a Plugin](#checklist-shipping-a-plugin)
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## Core Concepts
35: 
36: An Antigravity **plugin** is a namespaced, shareable bundle that packages **skills**, **rules**, **hooks**, and optionally **MCP server configs** and **sidecar definitions** into a single deployable unit. Plugins are the recommended way to distribute complex agent behaviours.
37: 
38: A plugin has two distinct concerns:
39: 
40: | Concern | Where it lives | Mutable? | Committed? |
41: |---------|---------------|:--------:|:----------:|
42: | **Plugin code** (scripts, skills, rules, hooks templates) | `.agents/plugins/<name>/` | ❌ Immutable | ✅ Submodule |
43: | **Instance state** (config, claims, cooldown files) | `.agents/plugins/<name>-workspace/` | ✅ Mutable | Config: ✅ / State: ❌ |
44: 
45: The plugin directory is a **git submodule** (or standalone clone). It is treated as read-only after installation. All mutable state — configuration, runtime locks, circuit breaker files — lives in a separate **workspace directory** alongside it.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## Directory Layout
50: 
51: ### Standard Layout (Consumer Project)
52: 
53: ```
54: my-project/                                         ← REPO_DIR (derivable)
55: ├── .agents/
56: │   ├── plugins/
57: │   │   ├── bug-fixer-loop-plugin/                  ← PLUGIN_DIR (git submodule, immutable)
58: │   │   │   ├── plugin.json                         ← Manifest (required by Antigravity)
59: │   │   │   ├── hooks.json                          ← Hook templates with <plugin_dir> placeholders
60: │   │   │   ├── rules/
61: │   │   │   │   └── AGENTS.md                       ← Plugin rules (generic, not project-specific)
62: │   │   │   ├── scripts/
63: │   │   │   │   ├── install.sh
64: │   │   │   │   ├── uninstall.sh
65: │   │   │   │   ├── configure.sh
66: │   │   │   │   ├── tick_dispatcher.py
67: │   │   │   │   ├── triage_dispatcher.py
68: │   │   │   │   ├── trajectory_dispatcher.py
69: │   │   │   │   ├── safe_ingest.py
70: │   │   │   │   └── pre_tool_gate.py
71: │   │   │   ├── skills/
72: │   │   │   │   ├── bug-fixer-tick/SKILL.md
73: │   │   │   │   ├── bug-fixer-triage/SKILL.md
74: │   │   │   │   └── ...
75: │   │   │   ├── sidecars/                           ← Sidecar templates with placeholders
76: │   │   │   │   ├── bug-fixer-tick/sidecar.json
77: │   │   │   │   ├── bug-fixer-triage/sidecar.json
78: │   │   │   │   └── trajectory-review/sidecar.json
79: │   │   │   └── agents/
80: │   │   │       └── leak-auditor.md
81: │   │   │
82: │   │   └── bug-fixer-loop-workspace/               ← STATE_DIR (mutable, per-project)
83: │   │       ├── config.json                         ← Instance config (committed ✅)
84: │   │       ├── .gitignore                          ← Ignores runtime state only
85: │   │       ├── claims/                             ← Lock files (gitignored)
86: │   │       ├── cooldown.json                       ← Circuit breaker state (gitignored)
87: │   │       └── failure_count                       ← Consecutive failure counter (gitignored)
88: │   │
89: │   ├── hooks.json                                  ← Workspace-scoped hooks (resolved paths)
90: │   └── rules/
91: │       ├── bug-fixer-AGENTS.md                     ← Plugin rules (installed here)
92: │       └── 05-pio-lock.md                          ← Project-specific rules (human-authored)
93: │
94: ├── src/
95: ├── docs/
96: └── ...
97: ```
98: 
99: ### Key Principle: Path Derivation
100: 
101: Every path is derivable from the config file's own location:
102: 
103: ```
104: config.json is at:  <repo>/.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/config.json
105:                      │
106:                      ├── parent     = STATE_DIR  (.../bug-fixer-loop-workspace/)
107:                      ├── parent²    = plugins/
108:                      ├── parent³    = .agents/
109:                      └── parent⁴   = REPO_DIR
110:                      
111:                      STATE_DIR sibling = PLUGIN_DIR (.../bug-fixer-loop-plugin/)
112: ```
113: 
114: This means `repo_dir` and `plugin_dir` **never need to be stored in config**. Scripts derive them at runtime:
115: 
116: ```python
117: CONFIG_FILE = Path("...workspace/config.json").resolve()
118: STATE_DIR = CONFIG_FILE.parent
119: REPO_DIR = STATE_DIR.parent.parent.parent
120: PLUGIN_DIR = STATE_DIR.parent / "bug-fixer-loop-plugin"
121: ```
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## Discovery & Loading
126: 
127: Antigravity discovers plugins by traversing the `.agents/plugins/` directory tree. Each plugin directory must contain a `plugin.json` manifest:
128: 
129: ```json
130: {
131:   "name": "bug-fixer-loop"
132: }
133: ```
134: 
135: When discovered and enabled, Antigravity automatically ingests:
136: - **Skills** from `plugins/<name>/skills/` (progressive disclosure — name + description loaded, full content on activation)
137: - **Rules** from `plugins/<name>/rules/` (merged into active rule set)
138: - **Hooks** from `plugins/<name>/hooks.json` (registered for lifecycle events)
139: - **MCP servers** from `plugins/<name>/mcp_config.json` (launched and tools exposed)
140: 
141: ### Loading Priority (highest → lowest)
142: 
143: 1. **Workspace project** — `.agents/` walking up from CWD to repo root
144: 2. **Declared configs** — explicit `skills.json` or `plugins.json`
145: 3. **Global discovery** — `~/.gemini/config/`
146: 4. **Built-in customisations** — bundled with Antigravity
147: 5. **Global declared configs** — global JSON configs
148: 
149: Workspace-scoped customisations always win over global ones.
150: 
151: ### Enabling / Disabling
152: 
153: Plugin state is recorded in `~/.gemini/config/config.json`:
154: 
155: ```json
156: {
157:   "plugins": {
158:     "bug-fixer-loop-plugin": { "enabled": true }
159:   }
160: }
161: ```
162: 
163: Toggle via CLI: `agy plugin enable bug-fixer-loop` / `agy plugin disable bug-fixer-loop`.
164: 
165: ---
166: 
167: ## The Immutable Plugin Root Principle
168: 
169: > **The plugin directory is read-only after installation.**
170: 
171: This is the single most important architectural rule. The plugin directory (`bug-fixer-loop-plugin/`) is typically a git submodule. Nothing should write to it:
172: 
173: - ❌ No `config.json` with instance values
174: - ❌ No runtime state files (claims, locks, cooldowns)
175: - ❌ No `install.sh` writing back into it
176: - ❌ No sed/templating modifying files in-place
177: 
178: Scripts, skills, and agents are **used in-place** — never copied to global directories. The plugin root is the single source of truth for code.
179: 
180: ---
181: 
182: ## Configuration Management
183: 
184: ### What Goes in `config.json`
185: 
186: The workspace config contains **project settings only** — no paths, no machine-specific values:
187: 
188: ```json
189: {
190:   "$schema": "bug-fixer-loop-config-v1",
191:   "target_repo": "owner/repo-name",
192:   "maintainer": "github-login",
193:   "trusted_users": [],
194:   "spec_file_path": "docs/design_specification.md",
195:   "protected_files": ["docs/design_specification.md"],
196:   "leak_patterns": ["ya29\\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", "AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"],
197:   "max_concurrent_prs": 4,
198:   "test_command": "pio test -e native",
199:   "lint_command": "",
200:   "pr_prefix": "[BugFixer]",
201:   "branch_prefix": "fix",
202:   "triage_cron": "0 * * * *",
203:   "tick_cron": "*/10 * * * *",
204:   "trajectory_review_cron": "0 18 * * *"
205: }
206: ```
207: 
208: This file is **committed to the consumer repo** — it documents the project's bug-fixer setup for the whole team.
209: 
210: ### What Gets Gitignored
211: 
212: Only runtime state is gitignored (via `.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/.gitignore`):
213: 
214: ```gitignore
215: claims/
216: cooldown.json
217: failure_count
218: triage_cooldown.json
219: triage_failure_count
220: ```
221: 
222: ### Config Discovery in Scripts
223: 
224: Scripts find the config through a standard search:
225: 
226: ```python
227: # Dispatchers (invoked from known location within plugin):
228: WORKSPACE_CONFIG = PLUGIN_DIR / "../../bug-fixer-loop-workspace/config.json"
229: 
230: # CLI tools (invoked from anywhere):
231: candidates = [
232:     plugin_dir.parent / "bug-fixer-loop-workspace" / "config.json",   # standard layout
233:     Path.cwd() / ".agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/config.json",  # cwd fallback
234: ]
235: 
236: # Override via environment:
237: BUG_FIXER_CONFIG=/path/to/config.json python3 scripts/safe_ingest.py ...
238: ```
239: 
240: ---
241: 
242: ## Hooks
243: 
244: Hooks are lifecycle interceptors that run external commands at specific points in the agent's execution. The plugin defines hooks in `hooks.json` with **placeholder paths**:
245: 
246: ```json
247: {
248:   "bug-fixer-file-gate": {
249:     "PreToolUse": [{
250:       "matcher": "write_to_file|replace_file_content",
251:       "hooks": [{
252:         "type": "command",
253:         "command": "python3 <plugin_dir>/scripts/pre_tool_gate.py",
254:         "timeout": 10
255:       }]
256:     }]
257:   }
258: }
259: ```
260: 
261: ### Path Resolution
262: 
263: The `<plugin_dir>` placeholder is resolved by `install.sh` at install time, producing a workspace-scoped `hooks.json` at `.agents/hooks.json`.
264: 
265: **Critical rule:** Hooks must be installed to the **workspace** `.agents/hooks.json`, never to the global `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`. A broken global hook bricks every project on the machine.
266: 
267: ### Hook Working Directory
268: 
269: The hook command's working directory is set to the directory containing `hooks.json`. If hooks are installed at `.agents/hooks.json`, the cwd is `.agents/`.
270: 
271: ### PreToolUse Contract
272: 
273: The `pre_tool_gate.py` hook receives tool call details on stdin and returns a decision on stdout:
274: 
275: ```json
276: // stdin (from Antigravity)
277: {
278:   "toolCall": {"name": "write_to_file", "args": {"TargetFile": "/path/to/file.py"}},
279:   "conversationId": "...",
280:   "workspacePaths": ["/path/to/repo"]
281: }
282: 
283: // stdout (from hook script)
284: {"decision": "allow"}     // or "deny" with "reason"
285: ```
286: 
287: ---
288: 
289: ## Rules
290: 
291: Plugin rules live at `plugins/<name>/rules/AGENTS.md`. They are **generic** — applicable to any project using the plugin.
292: 
293: **Project-specific rules** (e.g., PlatformIO MCP lock protocol, framework-specific testing rules) belong in the consumer project's `.agents/rules/`, not in the plugin.
294: 
295: Example separation:
296: 
297: | Rule | Where | Why |
298: |------|-------|-----|
299: | "Never auto-merge PRs" | Plugin `rules/AGENTS.md` | Universal to all bug-fixer consumers |
300: | "Use PlatformIO MCP for builds" | Consumer `.agents/rules/05-pio-lock.md` | Only applies to PlatformIO projects |
301: | "Run `npm test` before PRs" | Consumer `.agents/rules/` | Only applies to Node.js projects |
302: 
303: The plugin's Step 9 (Verify) defers to project rules:
304: > *"Respect any project-level rules about build/test tooling. If the project rules mandate using MCP server tools instead of CLI commands, follow them."*
305: 
306: ---
307: 
308: ## Skills
309: 
310: Skills are multi-step agent procedures defined in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. They are **used in-place** from the plugin directory — never copied to global config.
311: 
312: Antigravity discovers skills via progressive disclosure:
313: 1. Only the skill's **name and description** (from YAML frontmatter) are loaded into context
314: 2. The **full content** is loaded only when the agent or user activates the skill
315: 
316: ### Skill Path References
317: 
318: Skills reference plugin scripts using `PLUGIN_DIR`, which is resolved at runtime:
319: 
320: ```markdown
321: ## Step 0: Configuration Guard
322: PLUGIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "<this_skill_file>")/../.." && pwd)"
323: STATE_DIR="<workspace_root>/.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace"
324: ```
325: 
326: ---
327: 
328: ## Sidecars & Dispatchers
329: 
330: Sidecars are **background processes managed by Antigravity's runtime**. They are the mechanism for running recurring automated tasks — scheduled builds, periodic issue triage, cron-driven health checks — without requiring a user to be actively chatting.
331: 
332: ### How Antigravity Discovers Sidecars
333: 
334: Antigravity scans specific directories on startup for `sidecar.json` files:
335: 
336: ```
337: ~/.gemini/antigravity/sidecars/<name>/sidecar.json    ← Antigravity 2.0
338: ~/.gemini/jetski/sidecars/<name>/sidecar.json          ← Jetski / IDE
339: ```
340: 
341: > **These directories are inherently global.** There is no workspace-scoped sidecar discovery. This is the one place where the "nothing outside the plugin" rule can't fully apply — sidecars must be written to these runtime directories or Antigravity won't find them.
342: 
343: Each `<name>/` subdirectory represents one sidecar process. Antigravity reads the `sidecar.json` manifest and manages the process lifecycle.
344: 
345: ### Sidecar Manifest (`sidecar.json`)
346: 
347: A sidecar manifest defines what to run, how to schedule it, and what environment to provide:
348: 
349: ```json
350: {
351:   "builtin": "schedule",
352:   "args": ["*/10 * * * *", "/path/to/scripts/tick_dispatcher.py"],
353:   "restart_policy": "always",
354:   "display_name": "Bug Fixer Tick (owner/repo)",
355:   "description": "Checks for eligible issues every 10 min.",
356:   "env": {
357:     "ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID": "project-uuid",
358:     "PATH": "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:...",
359:     "BUG_FIXER_CONFIG": "/path/to/workspace/config.json"
360:   }
361: }
362: ```
363: 
364: | Field | Type | Description |
365: |-------|------|-------------|
366: | `builtin` | string | The sidecar type. `"schedule"` runs on a cron schedule. |
367: | `args` | array | For `schedule`: `[cron_expression, script_path]`. The script is invoked by the scheduler on each cron tick. |
368: | `restart_policy` | string | `"always"` restarts the sidecar if it crashes. |
369: | `display_name` | string | Human-readable name shown in the Antigravity UI/dashboard. |
370: | `description` | string | Shown in sidecar listings. |
371: | `env` | object | Environment variables injected into the process. **Critical** — see below. |
372: 
373: ### Sidecar Execution Model
374: 
375: When a `schedule` sidecar fires:
376: 
377: 1. **Antigravity's scheduler** wakes up at the cron interval
378: 2. **Forks a subprocess** running the script specified in `args[1]`
379: 3. The script runs as a **plain Python process** — it is NOT an LLM conversation
380: 4. The script's `stdout`/`stderr` go to Antigravity's sidecar logs
381: 5. The script is expected to **exit quickly** (seconds, not minutes)
382: 6. If the script needs to do LLM work, it spawns a **new conversation** via `agentapi new-conversation`
383: 7. The `restart_policy: "always"` means the scheduler continues firing on the next cron tick even if the script exits with an error
384: 
385: ### The `env` Block is Critical
386: 
387: **Sidecars do NOT inherit the user's shell environment.** The sidecar process gets a minimal environment from Antigravity's runtime. Without an explicit `env` block:
388: 
389: - **`PATH` is minimal** — `agentapi`, `python3`, `gh`, and other CLI tools won't be found
390: - **`ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` is unset** — `agentapi new-conversation` fails because it doesn't know which project to spawn into
391: - **`BUG_FIXER_CONFIG` is unset** — scripts can't find the workspace config
392: 
393: This was the root cause of a production failure: the sidecar templates shipped without `env`, so the installed sidecars pointed to scripts that couldn't find `agentapi` on the `PATH`. All 9 sidecar configs (3 sidecars × 3 directories) were silently failing on every cron tick.

395: #### Required `env` Variables

399: | `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` | Identifies the project for `agentapi` conversation spawning | Detected at install time from `~/.gemini/config/projects/*.json` or from the active Antigravity context |
400: | `PATH` | Full `PATH` including `~/.gemini/antigravity/bin/` (for `agentapi`) and `/usr/local/bin` (for `python3`, `gh`) | Snapshot of `$PATH` at install time |

462: ### Dispatcher Architecture (The Non-LLM Control Plane)
463: 
464: Dispatchers are the Python scripts invoked by sidecars. They are **pure control plane logic** — they never call the LLM themselves. Their sole job is to decide whether there's work to do and, if so, spawn an LLM conversation to handle it.
465: 
466: #### Why This Matters
467: 
468: Running an LLM conversation costs money and burns quota. If the sidecar directly launched an LLM conversation on every cron tick, you'd spend tokens even when there's nothing to do. The dispatcher pattern keeps costs at zero when idle:
469: 
470: ```
471: Cron fires → Dispatcher runs  → No eligible issues → Exit immediately (cost: $0)
472: Cron fires → Dispatcher runs  → 2 eligible issues  → Spawn 2 conversations (cost: ~$0.50)
473: ```
474: 
475: #### Dispatcher Flow (Tick — the most complex)
476: 
477: ```
478: 1.  Load config from workspace (WORKSPACE_CONFIG only — no plugin root fallback)
479: 2.  Derive REPO_DIR, STATE_DIR, PLUGIN_DIR from config file location
480: 3.  Check circuit breaker — if cooldown.json exists and not expired, exit immediately
481: 4.  Recover stale claims (3-layer detection):
482:     a. Claim file exists but has no conversation_id (spawn failed mid-write)
483:     b. Claim file older than TTL (conversation ran too long or was killed)
484:     c. Conversation exists but is in terminal state (idle/errored/cancelled)
485: 5.  Count active bug-fixer PRs via safe_ingest.py — if >= max_concurrent, exit
486: 6.  Query GitHub for eligible issues (via safe_ingest.py):
487:     - Has "auto-fixable" label
488:     - Not in exclusion_labels (e.g., "human-required", "P1-blocker", "hardware-required")
489:     - Not already claimed (no active claim file)
490:     - Sorted by priority (milestone boost, label priority ranking)
491: 7.  For each eligible issue (up to max_concurrent - active_prs):
492:     a. Write claim file to STATE_DIR/claims/<issue_number>.json (atomic lock)
493:     b. Add "status:in-progress" label to the GitHub issue
494:     c. Build the skill prompt (read SKILL.md, inject config values)
495:     d. Spawn LLM conversation via: agentapi new-conversation --system-prompt <skill> --user-prompt <issue>
496:     e. Capture conversation_id from agentapi stdout
497:     f. Update claim file with conversation_id
498:     g. If spawn fails: remove claim file, remove label, log error
499: 8.  Track spawn success/failure for circuit breaker
500: 9.  Log summary and exit
501: ```
502: 
503: #### Spawning Conversations via `agentapi`
504: 
505: The dispatchers use `agentapi new-conversation` to launch LLM sessions:
506: 
507: ```python
508: cmd = [
509:     "agentapi", "new-conversation",
510:     "--system-prompt", skill_text,
511:     "--user-prompt", prompt_text,
512: ]
513: r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
514: ```
515: 
516: The `agentapi` tool is Antigravity's CLI for programmatic conversation management. It:
517: - Creates a new conversation in the Antigravity runtime
518: - Injects the skill as the system prompt
519: - Injects the issue details as the user prompt
520: - Returns a JSON object with `conversationId` that can be used to monitor progress
521: - Requires `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` to know which project context to use
522: 
523: A successful spawn returns:
524: ```json
525: {"conversationId": "ec33ebf9-0cba-4100-8142-c61503f6c587"}
526: ```
527: 
528: A failed spawn (quota exhausted, missing env vars, etc.) returns a non-zero exit code and error text on stderr.
529: 
530: #### Stale Claim Recovery
531: 
532: The tick dispatcher implements 3-layer stale claim detection to handle conversations that crash, timeout, or are killed:
533: 
534: ```python
535: # Layer 1: Claim file has no conversation ID (spawn failed mid-write)
536: if not claim_data.get("conversation_id"):
537:     recover(claim)
538: 
539: # Layer 2: Claim file older than TTL (conversation ran too long)
540: if claim_age > CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS:
541:     recover(claim)
542: 
543: # Layer 3: Conversation exists but is in terminal state
544: status = get_conversation_status(conversation_id)
545: if status in ("idle", "errored", "cancelled"):
546:     recover(claim)
547: ```
548: 
549: Recovery means:
550: 1. Remove the claim file from `STATE_DIR/claims/`
551: 2. Remove the `status:in-progress` label from the GitHub issue
552: 3. The issue becomes eligible for the next tick cycle
553: 
554: #### Claim File Format
555: 
556: ```json
557: {
558:   "issue_number": 42,
559:   "conversation_id": "ec33ebf9-0cba-4100-8142-c61503f6c587",
560:   "claimed_at": "2026-09-27T14:30:00+00:00",
561:   "branch": "fix/42-sensor-timeout"
562: }
563: ```

567: ## Circuit Breakers
568: 
569: When the LLM quota runs out, dispatchers can enter a catastrophic failure loop:
570: 
571: 1. **Tick fires** (every 10 minutes)
572: 2. **Finds eligible issues**, writes claim files, adds `status:in-progress` labels
573: 3. **Spawns `agentapi new-conversation`** — all calls fail (quota exhausted)
574: 4. **Removes claim files**, removes labels (cleanup on failure)
575: 5. **Next tick fires** — same issues are eligible again
576: 6. **Labels churn** on GitHub (added/removed every 10 minutes), user is spammed with dozens of failing conversation notifications
577: 7. **Repeat indefinitely** until quota is restored or the sidecar is manually stopped
578: 
579: ### Implementation
580: 
581: Each dispatcher tracks consecutive spawn failures using two files in the workspace state directory:
582: 
583: | File | Purpose | Format |
584: |------|---------|--------|
585: | `failure_count` | Number of consecutive ticks where all spawns failed | Plain text integer |
586: | `cooldown.json` | Present only when cooling down | JSON with `reason`, `entered_at`, `expires_at`, `expires_at_iso` |
587: 
588: #### Startup Check
589: 
590: ```python
591: COOLDOWN_FILE = STATE_DIR / "cooldown.json"
592: FAILURE_COUNT_FILE = STATE_DIR / "failure_count"
593: MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 3
594: COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 3600  # 1 hour
595: 
596: # Circuit breaker: check cooldown before doing any work
597: if COOLDOWN_FILE.exists():
598:     try:
599:         cooldown = json.loads(COOLDOWN_FILE.read_text())
600:         if time.time() < cooldown.get("expires_at", 0):
601:             log(f"TICK_EXIT: Cooling down until {cooldown['expires_at_iso']} — "
602:                 f"reason: {cooldown['reason']}")
603:             sys.exit(0)
604:         # Cooldown expired, clean up and resume normal operation
605:         COOLDOWN_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
606:         FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
607:     except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
608:         COOLDOWN_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
609: ```
610: 
611: #### Post-Spawn Tracking
612: 
613: ```python
614: # After the spawn loop completes:
615: if spawned == 0 and len(eligible) > 0:
616:     # Had work to do but couldn't spawn anything — this is a failure
617:     try:
618:         count = int(FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.read_text().strip()) + 1 \
619:             if FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.exists() else 1
620:     except (ValueError, OSError):
621:         count = 1
622:     STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
623:     FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.write_text(str(count))
624:     if count >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES:
625:         expires = time.time() + COOLDOWN_SECONDS
626:         COOLDOWN_FILE.write_text(json.dumps({
627:             "reason": f"{count} consecutive spawn failures",
628:             "entered_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
629:             "expires_at": expires,
630:             "expires_at_iso": datetime.fromtimestamp(expires, timezone.utc).isoformat(),
631:         }))
632:         log(f"Circuit breaker tripped after {count} consecutive failures. "
633:             f"Cooling down for {COOLDOWN_SECONDS}s.")
634: else:
635:     # At least one spawn succeeded, or no eligible work — reset counter
636:     FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
637: ```
638: 
639: #### Cooldown File Format
640: 
641: ```json
642: {
643:   "reason": "3 consecutive spawn failures",
644:   "entered_at": "2026-09-27T14:30:00+00:00",
645:   "expires_at": 1727447400.0,
646:   "expires_at_iso": "2026-09-27T15:30:00+00:00"
647: }
648: ```
649: 
650: #### Behaviour Summary
651: 
652: | Tick # | Eligible Issues | Spawned | Failure Count | Action |
653: |:------:|:--------------:|:-------:|:-------------:|--------|
654: | 1 | 3 | 0 (quota fail) | 1 | Continue |
655: | 2 | 3 | 0 (quota fail) | 2 | Continue |
656: | 3 | 3 | 0 (quota fail) | 3 | **Trip breaker** — write `cooldown.json`, stop for 1 hour |
657: | 4–9 | — | — | — | Exit immediately (cooldown active) |
658: | 10 | 3 | 2 (quota restored) | 0 | Reset counter, normal operation resumes |
659: | 11 | 0 | 0 (no work) | 0 | No increment — counter only tracks "had work but couldn't do it" |

689: ### 1. Writing to Global Config
690: 
691: **Problem:** `install.sh` wrote hooks, rules, scripts, and skills to `~/.gemini/config/`. A broken global hook bricked every project on the machine. When an agent ran `git clean` and deleted the plugin directory, the global hook pointed to a missing script, blocking all tool execution across the entire installation.
692: 
693: **Fix:** Only write workspace-scoped artefacts. Scripts and skills are used in-place.
694: 
695: ### 2. Absolute Paths in Config
696: 
697: **Problem:** `config.json` contained `/Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/...` — completely non-portable. Can't be committed, can't be shared.
698: 
699: **Fix:** Derive paths from the config file's own location. The standardised directory layout makes every path computable at runtime.

701: ### 3. Instance Values in Plugin Root
702: 
703: **Problem:** `config.json` with `target_repo`, `repo_dir`, and `maintainer` lived in the plugin root. This meant:
704: - Dirty submodule after configuration
705: - Instance values committed to the plugin repo
706: - Only one project could use the plugin at a time
707: 
708: **Fix:** Config lives in the workspace directory (sibling of the plugin submodule). Plugin root contains no instance-specific files.
709: 
710: ### 4. No Circuit Breaker
711: 
712: **Problem:** When LLM quota ran out, the tick dispatcher fired every 10 minutes, spawned conversations that all failed, churned issue labels on GitHub, and spammed the user with failing conversations.
713: 
714: **Fix:** Track consecutive spawn failures. After 3 failures, write a cooldown file and stop ticking for 1 hour.

716: ### 5. Project-Specific Rules in Generic Plugin
717: 
718: **Problem:** Rule 16 ("PlatformIO MCP Lock Discipline") was in the plugin's `rules/AGENTS.md`. Every consumer — including Node.js, Rails, or plain Python projects — inherited a PlatformIO-specific rule.

720: **Fix:** Replace with a generic "Respect Project Testing Rules" rule. PlatformIO specifics go in the consumer's `.agents/rules/`.

722: ### 6. Copying Files Instead of Using In-Place
723: 
724: **Problem:** `install.sh` copied skills to `~/.gemini/config/skills/` AND `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/`, with `sed` templating to bake in absolute paths. This created 12+ duplicate skill directories that drifted out of sync with the source.

726: **Fix:** Skills are used directly from the plugin directory. Antigravity discovers them via the plugin's `plugin.json` manifest.

730: **Problem:** Sidecar templates had no `env` field. The sidecar scheduler doesn't inherit the user's shell `PATH`, so `agentapi` couldn't be found.

30: ## Review Rubric: Core Pillars of Scrutiny
31: 
32: Scrutinize every line of the PR diff against these four pillars:
33: 
34: ### 1. Technical Debt & Design Integrity
35: - **Root-cause vs. symptom patching:** Does the fix address the underlying bug or merely suppress an error/symptom?
36: - **Improper coupling & layering:** Does the fix violate layer boundaries (e.g., UI or high-level logic reaching directly into low-level drivers or hardware abstractions)?
37: - **Workarounds & hacks:** Are there ad-hoc flags, global state additions, arbitrary `sleep()` or timeout increases, or copy-pasted logic?
38: - **Code cleanliness & idioms:** Does the implementation follow modern idiomatic language patterns (e.g., C++17/C++20, RAII, const-correctness, noexcept specifications) and project naming conventions?
39: 
40: ### 2. Pointer Instability & Lifetime Safety
41: - **Dangling pointers & references:** Are pointers or references returned or stored that outlive the referenced object (e.g., returning reference to stack local)?
42: - **Use-after-free / Use-after-move:** Are objects accessed after being moved from, freed, or deleted?
43: - **Null / nullptr dereferences:** Are pointer parameters or return values dereferenced without validation?
44: - **Iterator & reference invalidation:** Does the code modify containers (vectors, maps, lists) while iterating over them or holding element references?
45: - **Unsafe casting:** Are there raw `reinterpret_cast` or C-style casts bypassing type safety?
46: 
47: ### 3. Memory Leaks & Resource Management
48: - **Heap allocation lifecycle:** Are all dynamic allocations (`malloc`, `new`, `calloc`) properly matched with deallocations (`free`, `delete`), or managed via RAII smart pointers (`std::unique_ptr`, `std::shared_ptr`)?
49: - **Early returns & error paths:** If a function exits early on an error or validation failure, are allocated buffers, locks, or descriptors properly cleaned up?
50: - **Resource handle leaks:** Are file descriptors, network sockets, timers, mutexes, or OS handles closed/released under all execution paths?
51: - **Unbounded buffer growth:** Can buffers, queues, or caches grow without bounds under unexpected input?
52: - **Circular references:** Do `std::shared_ptr` instances create reference cycles preventing reclamation?
53: 
54: ### 4. Missed Architectural Constraints & Concurrency
55: - **Specification alignment:** Does the change violate specifications defined in the project's design docs (e.g., `spec_file_path` or `additional_design_docs`)?
56: - **Public API & contract breakage:** Does the PR alter public function signatures, ABI stability, or expected semantics without deprecation?
57: - **Concurrency & thread safety:**
58:   - Are shared data structures accessed across threads or tasks without proper synchronization?
59:   - Are blocking operations invoked from asynchronous callbacks, event loops, or ISR contexts?
60:   - Could mutex acquisition order introduce lock inversion or deadlocks?
61: - **Execution context constraints:** In resource-constrained or embedded environments (e.g., ESP32/FreeRTOS), does the fix exceed stack limits or perform forbidden operations in interrupt contexts?

7: # Issue Management Process
8: 
9: GitHub Issues on **`matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin`** are the canonical
10: system of record for all plugin defects. This document tells you everything
11: you need to raise, track, link, and close a bug-fixer-loop issue.
12: 
13: ---
14: 
15: ## Plugin Issues vs Target Repo Issues
16: 
17: Not every problem belongs on the plugin repo. Use this table to decide where
18: to file:
19: 
20: | Symptom | File against |
21: |---|---|
22: | Triage misclassifies an issue (wrong tier) | `matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin` |
23: | `safe_ingest.py` false-positive redacts valid content | `matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin` |
24: | `pre_tool_gate.py` blocks a legitimate operation | `matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin` |
25: | Tick sidecar crashes, orphans a claim, or opens a broken PR | `matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin` |
26: | Trajectory review misidentifies a failure pattern | `matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin` |
27: | Test quality audit rubric is too strict/lenient | `matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin` |
28: | `configure.sh` or `install.sh` fails or misconfigures | `matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin` |
29: | Sidecar cron schedule is wrong or sidecars don't fire | `matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin` |
30: | A bug in the **target project's code** (not the plugin) | The target repo configured in `config.json` |
31: | A bug-fixer PR contains a wrong fix for a target repo issue | The target repo (review feedback on the PR) |
32: 
33: > **Rule of thumb:** If the problem is in *how the agent operates*, file it
34: > on the plugin repo. If the problem is in *what the agent produced*, address
35: > it via PR review on the target repo.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## Label Taxonomy
40: 
41: Apply labels at filing time. Every issue gets one severity label, plus any
42: applicable attribution/meta labels.
43: 
44: ### Severity (choose one)
45: 
46: | Label | When to use |
47: |---|---|
48: | `P1-blocker` | Plugin is non-functional — sidecars crash, claims orphan, PRs fail to open |
49: | `P2-correctness` | Plugin operates but produces wrong results — misclassification, incorrect exclusion zones, false-positive blocks |
50: | `P3-docs-dx` | Confusing docs, misleading skill instructions, cosmetic issues, unclear error messages |
51: | `P4-enhancement` | New capability or improvement — not a defect |
52: 
53: ### Component (apply all that fit)
54: 
55: | Label | When to use |
56: |---|---|
57: | `component:triage` | Bug is in the triage skill or triage sidecar logic |
58: | `component:tick` | Bug is in the tick/fixer skill or tick sidecar logic |
59: | `component:trajectory` | Bug is in the trajectory review skill or sidecar |
60: | `component:safe-ingest` | Bug is in `safe_ingest.py` ingestion or redaction |
61: | `component:pre-tool-gate` | Bug is in `pre_tool_gate.py` hook enforcement |
62: | `component:install-config` | Bug is in `install.sh`, `configure.sh`, or `uninstall.sh` |
63: | `component:test-quality` | Bug is in the test quality audit rubric |
64: | `component:rules` | Bug relates to safety rules (AGENTS.md) being too strict/lenient |
65: 
66: ### Attribution / meta (apply all that fit)
67: 
68: | Label | When to use |
69: |---|---|
70: | `found-in:<target-repo-name>` | Issue was surfaced while the plugin operated against a specific target repo (e.g. `found-in:esp32-app-foundation`). Create the label if it doesn't exist yet. |
71: | `backfill` | Historical issue filed after the fix was already merged; close immediately |
72: 
73: > **Important for agents:** The `found-in:` label must match the target repo
74: > the plugin was operating against when the issue was discovered. Do not copy
75: > a label from an example without checking it matches your context.
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## How to File an Issue
80: 
81: ### Identity Rule
82: 
83: File under whatever GitHub identity your `gh` CLI is currently authenticated
84: as — that is your true author identity for this action. Before filing, confirm
85: which account that is:
86: 
87: ```bash
88: gh auth status
89: # Shows which account you will file as. Make sure it is correct.
90: ```
91: 
92: Do not attempt to impersonate another user. File as yourself.
93: 
94: ### Issue Title Format
95: 
96: ```
97: [Component] One-line description of the defect
98: ```
99: 
100: Examples:
101: - `[safe_ingest] Maintainer approval gate rejects issues with unicode titles`
102: - `[triage] Small-scope override not applied to doc-only issues in security module`
103: - `[tick] Orphaned claim not cleaned up when transcript is missing`
104: - `[install] configure.sh fails silently when gh CLI is not authenticated`
105: 
106: ### Issue Body Template
107: 
108: ```markdown
109: ## Symptom
110: <!-- What goes wrong. What the user or agent sees or doesn't see. -->
111: 
112: ## Evidence
113: <!-- File paths, line numbers, error output, sidecar logs. -->
114: <!-- Format: `scripts/safe_ingest.py:142` -->
115: 
116: ## Transcript Context
117: <!-- If the issue was discovered during a sidecar run, include:
118:      - Conversation ID of the affected session
119:      - Relevant transcript excerpt (last 5-10 steps)
120:      - Any error messages from the agent log -->
121: 
122: ## Config Context
123: <!-- Relevant fields from config.json that may affect reproduction. -->
124: <!-- Redact any secrets or tokens. -->
125: ```json
126: {
127:   "target_repo": "<repo>",
128:   "max_concurrent_prs": 1,
129:   "test_command": "<command>"
130: }
131: ```
132: 
133: ## Found Against Commit
134: <!-- The plugin commit SHA where the bug was confirmed. -->
135: `<SHA>`
136: 
137: ## Suggested Fix
138: <!-- Optional but helpful. Concrete enough to act on. -->
139: 
140: ## Consumer Context
141: <!-- Which target repo was the plugin operating against? -->
142: Found in: <target-repo-name>, <sidecar or session context>
143: ```
144: 
145: ### Filing Command
146: 
147: ```bash
148: gh issue create \
149:   --repo matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin \
150:   --title "[Component] Description" \
151:   --body-file issue-body.md \
152:   --label "P2-correctness,component:tick,found-in:<target-repo-name>"
153: ```
154: 
155: If the `found-in:` label does not exist on the repo yet, create it first:
156: 
157: ```bash
158: gh label create "found-in:<target-repo-name>" \
159:   --repo matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin \
160:   --color "a855f7" \
161:   --description "Discovered while operating against <target-repo-name>"
162: ```
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## How Fixes Close Issues
167: 
168: The fixing PR's description must include:
169: 
170: ```
171: Fixes #N
172: ```
173: 
174: GitHub auto-closes the issue when the PR merges to `main`. No manual closing
175: is needed for issues resolved this way.
176: 
177: ---
178: 
179: ## Backfill Convention
180: 
181: When a defect was fixed before a GitHub issue was created (e.g. discovered
182: retrospectively from a PR or audit):
183: 
184: 1. File the issue using the standard body template.
185: 2. Add the `backfill` label alongside the severity and component labels.
186: 3. In the body, include: `**Resolved in:** commit \`<SHA>\`` (or PR #M).
187: 4. **Immediately close** the issue with reason "completed".
188: 
189: This preserves history and lets consumers link their context to a real
190: issue number without leaving a ghost open issue on the board.
191: 
192: ```bash
193: # Create a backfill issue and immediately close it
194: NUM=$(gh issue create \
195:   --repo matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin \
196:   --title "[Component] Description" \
197:   --body-file body.md \
198:   --label "P2-correctness,component:tick,found-in:<target-repo-name>,backfill" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$')
199: 
200: gh issue close "$NUM" \
201:   --repo matthewmcneill/bug-fixer-loop-plugin \
202:   --reason completed \
203:   --comment "Resolved in commit \`<SHA>\` (merged in PR #M, <date>)."
204: ```

35: - **Required:** Any change to security scripts (`safe_ingest.py`,
36:   `pre_tool_gate.py`), safety rules (`AGENTS.md`), new skills/sidecars,
37:   or changes affecting the triage tier classification logic.
38: - **Optional:** Documentation fixes, skill wording improvements, small
39:   isolated bug fixes with no security or classification impact.

44: `P4-enhancement` label.

53:

73: modified by autonomous agents:

76: |---|---|

95: feat/add-milestone-inheritance-to-triage

100: 
101: Always branch from the latest `origin/main`. Never branch from another
102: contributor's feature branch.

104: ### Issue Linking
105: 
106: The PR description body must include `Fixes #N` referencing the parent issue
107: so GitHub auto-closes it upon merge.

110: 
111: All tests must pass before opening a PR:
112: 
113: ```bash

115: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
116: ```
117: 
118: Include the full test output in the PR description body.
119: 
120: If you add or modify a script, add corresponding test coverage in `tests/`.
121: The existing test files provide patterns to follow:
122: - [`tests/test_safe_ingest.py`](../../tests/test_safe_ingest.py) — ingestion/redaction tests
123: - [`tests/test_pre_tool_gate.py`](../../tests/test_pre_tool_gate.py) — hook enforcement tests
